partners.mechanism_chain: SLC19A3 (HGNC:10600) —DECREASES→ Biotin (CHEBI:16748); Biotin (CHEBI:16748) —DISRUPTS→ Biotin-dependent carboxylase activity (GO:0006633); Biotin-dependent carboxylase activity (GO:0006633) —LEADS_TO→ Basal ganglia degeneration (HP:0002132); TPK1 (HGNC:11795) —DECREASES→ Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) (CHEBI:17608); Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) (CHEBI:17608) —DISRUPTS→ Thiamine-dependent enzyme activity (GO:0004253); Thiamine-dependent enzyme activity (GO:0004253) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0011445). Loss-of-function mutations in SLC19A3 lead to impaired biotin uptake and thus reduced availability of biotin, which is a cofactor for biotin-dependent carboxylases essential for neuronal function. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in TPK1 lead to reduced production of thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP), the active form of thiamine, which is a cofactor for several key enzymes in carbohydrate metabolism, including those in the citric acid cycle and pentose phosphate pathway, crucial for neuronal energy production. Both impaired biotin-dependent carboxylase activity and thiamine-dependent enzyme activity result in downstream neurological dysfunction, manifesting as basal ganglia degeneration and encephalopathy, respectively, highlighting a convergence on critical metabolic pathways for neuronal health.
